_comment: THE SERVER-GENERATED CLIENT ITEM CACHE. The client caches every SMSG_ITEM_QUERY_SINGLE_RESPONSE it ever receives in Cache\WDB\<locale>\itemcache.wdb and never expires an entry, so anyone who saw an item before we changed it keeps the stale copy forever -- report #224 (blank icons on items whose displayid and texture are both correct on our side) is exactly that. Server/azerothcore-wotlk/tools/wdb/gen_itemcache.py rebuilds the file from the live item_template, byte-for-byte the way the worldserver would have serialised it, and the launcher installs it. Not in payload/ and not in git: 1.7 MB of generated binary that changes every time an item does.
_off_switch: ★ ROLLBACK IS ONE EDIT: set enabled to false here, regenerate the manifest, push. New-Manifest.ps1 then writes no itemCache block, and WdbCache falls straight through to wiping Cache\WDB and installing nothing -- which is exactly what the launcher did before this feature existed. Every client returns to the known-good state on its next launch, with no launcher release. Rolling forward again is setting it back to true; clients that took the rollback lost their sentinel along with the cache and reinstall, and clients that never launched during the window are already holding this epoch and correctly do nothing.
_epoch: The trigger, and it is NOT a hash. THE CLIENT REWRITES itemcache.wdb CONTINUOUSLY DURING PLAY -- it appends every new query response -- so its hash stops matching whatever we installed within seconds of the player logging in and never matches again. Hash-based change detection would re-download this file on every single launch, forever. The launcher records the epoch it installed in a sentinel file (uncapped-itemcache.epoch) beside the cache and compares that instead. Bump the epoch whenever you publish new bytes; it is opaque, so any different string works, but keep it equal to the version in the filename so a client's sentinel names the file it is holding.
_publishing: publish.sh CANNOT publish this -- it regex-rejects any name that is not patch-enUS-<X>-<version>.MPQ -- so, like UncappedCT.dll, it is scp'd into /srv/uncapped-patches/public/ by hand and none of publish.sh's guards apply. Published filenames are IMMUTABLE: never overwrite one, always cut a new dated name. See PUBLISHING-PATCHES.md.
_locales: The generator writes an enUS locale into the WDB header and builds names from the base item_template columns, because item_template_locale has no enUS rows. None of that is right for a deDE client, and no client has been observed loading a cache whose header locale disagrees with its own. Anything not listed here gets the old wipe-only behaviour rather than a guess.
_built: 2026-08-17 from live item_template: 47652 records, 20.99 MiB raw, 1.74 MiB gzipped. Cut for report #929 -- the SAME half-fix shape as the #890b entry preserved below, and worth noting it recurred within a day. Scroll of Bounty (500204) still advertised '25%' after the owner cut the rate to 2.5% on 2026-08-16 (#899): the unit change moved the chat line, the SCRACC wire field and the addon, but not item_template.description, and the client never expires an item entry -- so every player who had already seen the scroll was reading a tooltip promising TEN TIMES what it pays. The description also now names what the scroll actually covers (mob-dropped trade goods and gems, and fishing pools), which it has done since #715 without saying so. The world-DB UPDATE was applied BEFORE generating, which is the ordering that matters: generate first and you publish the old text. Verified in the generated bytes before publishing -- the new string is present and the old '25%' string is absent (grep -ac on the raw .wdb: 1 and 0), and contentSize moved 22011684 -> 22011739, exactly the 55 bytes the longer description adds. All three DBC inputs (Item, Spell, SpellCategory) were re-copied out of the running container immediately before generating rather than reused from the Aug 11 copies on disk. The verifier was run against a real client cache and its negative control (--perturb Delay) was run too and DID fail, so the pass means something: 154 items differ from that old client file and every differing field was re-queried on live prod and matches what we generated -- Bloodpetal Sprout stackable 65535, Argent Warhorse RequiredLevel 0, Keystone MaxCount 0 / DisplayInfoID 4287, Hearthstone spellcooldown 900000, Ravager Flesh spellid 900087. PREVIOUS ENTRY, kept because its lesson is the same one: 2026-08-16 from live item_template: 47652 records, 20.99 MiB raw, 1.73 MiB gzipped. REGENERATED for report #890b -- a HALF-FIX that had been live for two days. The 2026-08-14 revision rev_20260814_614_fury_2h_haste_correction.sql dropped stat_value4 on the two new fury 2-handers (500230 Ruinblade of the Sundered Wake, 500231 Direhymn Verse of the Last Charge) from 10000 to 150. It was applied to the DB and was correct there -- and it had NEVER reached a single client, because itemcache.wdb is only replaced when the EPOCH moves and the epoch had sat at 2026.08.11a ever since. On this realm haste IS crit damage, so every player was reading a tooltip overstating those weapons by 66x. Verified in the generated file before publishing by decoding the payloads directly: entry 500230 carries stat_type 36 = 150 at payload offset 158, and 500231 the same at 162 -- not 10000. Record count 47649 -> 47652 (Scroll of Contagion 500211 and the two weapons), which is the independent check that this was built from current data rather than re-published from cache. Generator inputs verified current first: Item.dbc, SpellCategory.dbc and ItemSet.dbc were sha256-matched byte-for-byte against the running container before generating, and the TSVs were re-fetched from live. gzip written with mtime=0 so the archive is reproducible from the same input. Uploaded BY HAND to /srv/uncapped-patches/public -- publish.sh regex-rejects any name that is not patch-enUS-<X>-<version>.MPQ, so none of its guards apply here; the on-disk sha256 and an nginx 200 with the right byte count were checked manually instead. That manual path is what produced the 2026-08-09 DLL desync, so it is verified rather than assumed.
